cim: Teleperformance's latest results spotlight Africa's AI opportunity
cim_eredeti: Teleperformance's latest results spotlight Africa's AI opportunity
szoveg_eredeti:
As artificial intelligence reshapes the global business services industry, Teleperformance's latest financial results highlight a broader transformation. Across Africa, the French multinational is expanding its operations while investing in technology-enabled services and workforce capabilities.

Teleperformance's third-quarter results, published on November 5, offered a reminder of the challenges facing the global outsourcing industry.

The company, now operating under the TP brand, revised its 2026 revenue outlook to a decline of 1.5% to 2.5% on a like-for-like basis, reflecting pressure on traditional activities, particularly content moderation.Yet the results also revealed a different trajectory outside those activities. Excluding Trust & Safety, TP recorded 2% like-for-like revenue growth during the quarter, highlighting the resilience of other business lines. For Africa, where business process outsourcing has become an important source of investment, employment and services exports, the industry's technological transformation presents both opportunities and challenges.

TP has established a substantial presence across the continent, operating in 11 African countries with more than 50,000 employees and over 50 delivery sites.

Egypt provides a particularly striking example. According to Arab Finance's coverage of Egypt's expanding outsourcing industry, TP employs approximately 26,800 people in the country, generating 90% of its local revenues from exported services.Those exports reached €280 million in 2025 and are projected to grow to €344 million in 2026.The company has also outlined plans to create 18,000 additional jobs in Egypt under its expansion programme. These ambitions illustrate how African economies are becoming increasingly integrated into global technology and business services value chains.

The latest TP results suggest that artificial intelligence is moving rapidly from experimentation into commercial deployment.

At the end of September, the company reported approximately 1,400 AI projects worldwide, more than double the previous year's level, with over 300 new production-grade deployments during the third quarter. More than 35% of its global client portfolio now uses TP.ai solutions.

For African delivery centres, the implications extend beyond traditional customer support.AI-enabled operations increasingly require multilingual specialists, technical supervision, data expertise and employees capable of managing complex interactions.The opportunity is to move towards higher-value services, although automation also raises questions about the future of routine roles and workforce reskilling.

Africa's traditional outsourcing advantages include multilingual talent, competitive operating costs and proximity to European markets. The next phase could increasingly depend on combining those strengths with technological capabilities. TP's global financial outlook remains challenging, but the group has maintained its 2026 profitability and cash-flow targets while accelerating its AI transformation. For Africa's outsourcing economies, the broader lesson is clear: future competitiveness will depend not simply on supplying labour, but on developing the skills and technological infrastructure required to deliver increasingly sophisticated digital services.Teleperformance's African footprint provides a substantial platform from which to participate in that transition.
